source_files.role: Public installed API: open-mode enum, deleted default constructor, owning constructor/destructor, five database operations. No SQLite native type is exposed.
Constructor/open/close and all five public forwarding/query operations; private helper implementations read as source context.

Explicitly non-installed implementation header. Native handles, statement helpers, clearSignBit, SqlState and extraction helpers are private implementation context, not a second public-header coverage target.
Eight START_SECTION blocks and seventeen assertion macros. Database contents are built in the test; no external input or retained C++ output fixture exists.
Public SqliteConnector.h registration at95 and private SqliteConnector_impl.h registration at166-175.

Pinned dependency contract used for source issue review: handle ownership after failed open, valid close handle, explicit byte lengths and signed64-bit integer access. Not a claim that this vendored SQLite version is the Rust bundled version.

source_anchors.operation: Construction forwards exactly once to openDatabase_.
Destructor closes the stored native handle; copying is not disabled by the public header.
Three enum cases select SQLite READONLY, READWRITE, or READWRITE|CREATE flags; failure throws SqlOperationFailed.
countTableRows builds SELECT count(*) using raw table text, steps once and reads int64; prepare errors actually throw IllegalArgument despite the public SqlOperationFailed comment.
columnExists uses PRAGMA table_info and exact strcmp on the returned column names; unknown table yields no rows.
tableExists queries sqlite_master type table and name literal; views and the temporary schema are not included.
executeStatement calls sqlite3_exec with no row callback; it can process multiple SQL statements and does not create an implicit transaction.
prepareStatement calls sqlite3_prepare_v2 and discards the tail pointer; binding executes only the first prepared statement.
executeBindStatement binds each std::string as a BLOB using its byte length and ordinalk+1, then requires SQLITE_DONE; absent bindings remain NULL, excess bindings cause an error.
Private string extraction constructs a C string without sqlite3_column_bytes; not ported as a public operation.
Private extractValueIntStr selects sqlite3_column_int; not ported as a public operation.
Installed countTableRows documentation promises SqlOperationFailed for an unknown table; actual prepare path and class test disagree.
Unknown table UNKNOWN must throw IllegalArgument according to the source class test; source-reviewed expectation, not executed C++.

evidence: Tier3 source review for all8class-test sections and17macros, mapped to eight named native tests. All19 native tests and implementation reviewed. No full OpenMS C++ SDK build/execution or upstream-class-test execution. A separate tier2 adapted C++ probe compiled exact pinned connector code with explicit support substitutes and system SQLite3.45.1, reproducing CPP184/185 and the CPP189 exception mismatch; hashed external artifacts listed. Native test execution is recorded in docs/VALIDATION.md, not inferred from mapping. Other native boundary assertions are tier4 independently derived; bundled SQLite Rust execution alone is not an OpenMS C++ differential.
gaps: No full OpenMS C++ SDK differential or upstream-class-test execution; the executed probe uses explicitly listed support adapters and a host SQLite shared library.
S0 excludes the non-installed helper API and does not claim SqMass, OSW, OMS, MzMLSqlite or SQLite FileHandler dispatch completion.
Raw SQL execution deliberately has no wrapper work/memory/time budget or implicit transaction. Caller-controlled SQL may change a database before reporting an error.
Bindings execute only the first prepared statement and ignore trailing SQL, matching pinned source. SQLite failures map to Error::Io rather than preserving C++ exception class distinctions.
external_reference_note: Adapted C++ probe on kim. Exact pinned SqliteConnector.cpp/.h/_impl.h and sqlite3.h declarations; small support substitutes for StandardTypes, Exception and StringUtils. Host SQLite3.45.1 shared library. Not full OpenMS SDK include/link closure or original exception ABI.

adapted_cpp_probe.scope: Adapted C++ probe on kim. Exact pinned SqliteConnector.cpp/.h/_impl.h and sqlite3.h declarations; small support substitutes for StandardTypes, Exception and StringUtils. Host SQLite3.45.1 shared library. Not full OpenMS SDK include/link closure or original exception ABI.

execution.linkage: Host system libsqlite3.so.0; development headers absent, exact pinned SQLite declaration header used. No SQLite implementation source compiled and no library downloaded.

CPP-184: The ordinary table T exists; ABSENT does not.
The existing table named odd'name causes IllegalArgument during preparation.
The absent literal name "ABSENT' OR 1=1 --" incorrectly returns true.
The existing table named "odd table" causes preparation errors in both row-count and column-existence queries.
CPP-185: After a warm read returns 3 rows, a second connection holds BEGIN EXCLUSIVE.
A direct trace records successful preparation (SQLITE_OK, 0) followed by SQLITE_BUSY (5) at step.
Both tableExists(T) and columnExists(T, ID) return false, with database error code 5.
countTableRows(T) throws the adapted SqlOperationFailed and leaves one outstanding statement, counted using sqlite3_next_stmt.
After the second connection rolls back, the count is again 3.
CPP-189: countTableRows(UNKNOWN) throws the adapted IllegalArgument from the exact pinned prepareStatement path, agreeing with the source class test and contradicting the installed header.
Substitute exception classes preserve distinct throw/catch paths; the original exception inheritance, ABI and metadata formatting are not exercised.

adapted_cpp_probe.native_comparison: Native code and regression cases reviewed: punctuation names are literal; query errors propagate and lock recovery is checked; error classes intentionally map to Error::Io. Runtime outcomes belong to the integration validation record.

native_policy_reviewed.errors: SQLite operation errors wrap as Error::Io retaining rusqlite cause; explicit native validation InvalidValue
native_policy_reviewed.execution: Drain every result row of each batch statement; caller controls transaction, no implicit rollback
native_policy_reviewed.binding: Byte-oriented &[&[u8]] BLOB bindings; execute only first prepared statement, ignore trailing SQL without preparing it; reject empty/comment-only binding input; reject embedded NUL in all SQL before execution
native_policy_reviewed.budgets: No additional wrapper runtime/memory budgets, per integrating primitive-wrapper design; higher-level adapters own policy

public_api_mapping.SqlOpenMode: ReadOnly/ReadWrite/ReadWriteOrCreate; Default=create; READONLY spelling alias has same ReadOnly counterpart
public_api_mapping.destructor: Owned private Connection; no Clone/Copy, no raw handle
